log.msg: reuse-vs-roll verdict: extended ext/Draggable's Sortable, not hand-rolled. Kept whole: pointer capture, the ghost, the placeholder, Escape-cancels, the drag-source inline-display fix (2026-08-19). Overridden: release() -- Sortable commits via item.move() against a core/Item tree, and TreeDrag's nodes are plain parent-less data (the parked design's own reason to need a moved() writer seam instead) -- so release()/locate()/show() are replaced wholesale. before()/row() assume a container's DIRECT children ARE the registered draggables (true for ext/Panel, ext/editor); false here -- a Tree row sits inside an <li> beside its own children <ul>, one layer removed -- so locate() is hand-rolled from the target row's own rect (a vertical band: branch middle = into, else before/after) instead of Sortable's $items container model. Net: about 40% of Sortable's own lines reused verbatim (pointer lifecycle), the rest replaced -- worth it, because the 40% is exactly the previously-debugged half.

lesson: the whole-row-handle trap, found before it shipped. Draggable.grab() calls start() on EVERY pointerdown with no movement threshold -- a plain click-to-select on a whole-row handle hides the row (display:none), the layout reflows under the still-hidden row, and release()'s hit-test can resolve to a NEIGHBOR row at the original click point, firing a spurious moved(). ext/Panel already dodges this ("the handle is the grip alone, never the bar") but the reason is not stated there -- traced it from Draggable.js's own grab()/start() order plus a live reflow measurement, not from a bug report. TreeDrag ships a dedicated grip (span.ux-tree-drag-grip) as the handle, separate from the row's own click-to-select, reusing the precedent rather than rediscovering it by shipping the bug first.

lesson: what the drag actually cost. TreeDrag.js is 130 lines total for three parts (TreeDrag, TreeDrag.Row, TreeDrag.Drag) plus two small pure helpers (contains, locate_parent) -- Tree.js and TreeKeys.js are UNTOUCHED, zero base changes, matching the exemplar bar. The third-named-subclass pattern held exactly like TreeKeys: one static replaced (Tree.Row -> TreeDragRow), Tree.Item and Tree.Row travel down the chain untouched, and this.tree.constructor.Row / .Drag resolve through the live class with nothing hand-wired. Cost that TreeKeys did not pay: TreeKeys needed zero new state because Tree already gave it rows-in-DOM-order; TreeDrag needed one new pure function (locate_parent) because nodes carry no parent pointer -- the read-only-data design (doc/decisions.md's own reason for the moved() seam) means every commit re-derives 'whose child is this' by walking the tree, never stores it.

assign.outcome:
**TreeDrag landed -- grip-drag reorder for ux/Tree, zero base changes.** A third named subclass (`TreeDrag extends Tree`, one static replaced) exactly as the parked design called it -- `Tree.js` and `TreeKeys.js` untouched.

![](drag-between-mid.png)

- [TreeDrag demo](/framework/ux/Tree/drag/) -- drag a row by its grip, drop into a folder or between siblings, Escape cancels, `moved(node, into, at)` printed live
- [ux/Tree](/framework/ux/Tree/) -- parent, re-verified clean - [keys](/framework/ux/Tree/keys/) -- keyboard roving re-verified intact
- [doc/decisions.md](/framework/ux/Tree/doc/decisions.md) -- the built-vs-designed delta, the reuse call with evidence, the grip trap found before it shipped

**Reuse verdict:** extended `ext/Draggable`'s `Sortable`, not hand-rolled -- kept pointer capture, the ghost, the placeholder and Escape-cancel (the previously-debugged half) whole; replaced `release()`/`locate()`/`show()` because Sortable's `$items`-container model and `item.move()` commit both assume a shape Tree's plain, parent-less node data and its row-inside-an-li-beside-its-own-ul layout don't have. `locate()` reads the target row's own rect instead: the middle band of a branch is "into", the rest is "before/after".

**Acceptance gate: 5/5 green, no parked failures.** (1) drop onto a folder appends inside -- [drag-into-mid.png](drag-into-mid.png), payload `{node:package.json, into:docs, at:1}`. (2) drop between siblings reorders, insertion line visible mid-drag -- [drag-between-mid.png](drag-between-mid.png), payload `{node:package.json, into:null, at:1}`. (3) Escape mid-drag leaves the tree byte-identical -- [drag-escape-mid.png](drag-escape-mid.png) / [drag-escape-after.png](drag-escape-after.png). (4) every payload cross-checked against the DOM. (5) `/framework/ux/Tree/` and `/keys/` re-verified at 360 + 3440: zero overflow, zero non-LiveReload console errors, one Enter-selects proof still passes.

**Found before it shipped:** a whole-row drag handle would have fired spurious `moved()` calls on a plain click-to-select (`Draggable.grab()` hides the row on every pointerdown, no movement threshold, and the reflow can shift the hit-test onto a neighbour) -- shipped a dedicated grip (`.ux-tree-drag-grip`) instead, the same precedent `ext/Panel`'s handle already set but never wrote down.

**Left:** drop-into an EMPTY closed folder relies on `node.children !== undefined` rather than the visible caret, untested against a demo case with one (logged, not gated). No ARIA (matches Tree's own parked verdict). TreeKeys interplay not attempted -- TreeDrag lands on Tree alone, as the brief's own cut-first order allowed.
